verdict.reasoning: Patient describes “really bad tummy ache… at the lower bottom of my belly” that started “a few days ago” and is “really getting worse with time.”
Pain location and severity: “lower… in my lower abdomen… in the middle… below [belly button]… It’s there all the time… Maybe 8 [out of 10].”
She reports “vaginal, sometime bleeding… light color” after her period “about two weeks. Three weeks ago,” and later clarifies the light pink bleeding is different from her period.
She states: “I feel nausea. Like, I feel like vomiting, but I don't. I get nauseated, but I don't vomit.”
History: “I was constipated for a week… this week it seems to be… fine now… I’m going to the toilet every day.”
Contraception: “I use it from last one year. Plan on… Implanon.” Doctor later: “your Implanon was just put in a year ago?” Patient: “Yes.”
When asked about periods on Implanon: Doctor: “do you have periods? Or are they sporadic?” Patient: “No, they are sporadic. Like not the time it changes.”
Sexual activity: Doctor: “Are you having sexual intercourse regularly?” Patient: “Yes… Four days ago. Sorry, I just had.”
Transcript confirms timing only: pregnancy test was “around like a month ago” and “not since you've had the abdominal pain,” but the result (negative) is never stated.
When asked about operations: “Anything else? Have you had any operations?” Patient: “No.”
Patient: “Yeah, I have allergy. I have Amy… Ammo. Excellent allergy.” The agent is unclear despite indicating an allergy.
Occupation: “And what's your job day to day?” Patient: “Yeah, I'm a teacher.”
Living situation: “And who do you live with at home?” Patient: “My husband and my husband's family.”
Social history: “And do you smoke or drink alcohol? You take any other drugs?” Patient: “No.”
Travel: “Have you been abroad recently?” Patient: “Yes… About a year… Oh, a year ago. Not recently? No.”
The transcript contains no physical examination findings or vital signs; only history is discussed and an exam is planned for a later face‑to‑face visit.
Assessment restates history: lower abdominal pain that is “in the middle… below [belly button],” “there all the time,” “really getting worse with time,” rated “Maybe 8.”

She has “light pink color” bleeding since her period stopped two weeks ago and notes “this is different… it's not really like dark,” while on Implanon with sporadic periods, supporting it being abnormal relative to usual menses.
Summarizes history: “I feel nausea… I get nauseated, but I don't vomit,” and prior constipation: “I was constipated for a week… this week it seems to be… fine now.”
Confirmed Implanon use for a year and a pregnancy test “around like a month ago… not since you've had the abdominal pain,” so current pregnancy status is indeed not known.
Plan: “we can arrange a face to face examination… in a clinic… Would you be happy to call the support line and arrange that appointment?”
Doctor: “we would need to do a pregnancy test today if possible… if it's positive, we need to see you straight away. So give us a call back.”
The doctor advises earlier review only if “it gets a lot worse or you're not holding any fluids down.” New fever, fainting, or other deterioration are not mentioned.
No medications or investigations are prescribed in the transcript; the plan is limited to arranging face‑to‑face exam and home pregnancy test with follow‑up based on results.
